newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: INTERVIEW - Paribas plans $1.0 bln Asia investments.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Paribas plans $1.0 bln Asia investments.

text.p: Banque Paribas plans to invest almost US$1.0 billion across the Asia-Pacific region over the next three years, its Asian regional director Alan Kokocinski said on Wednesday.
Kokocinski told Reuters the bank's strategy was to buy directly into large companies with good growth potential and which needed an infusion of capital for future expansion.
"The goal is to have US$1 billion worth of investments in Asia by the year 2000," Kokokinski said in an interview.
He said Banque Paribas, the investment banking arm of France's Groupe Paribas, currently had direct investments in the region of around $72 million.
"We want to invest in pre-IPO (initial public offering) companies. A typical size would be a stake of US$20-25 million, or about 10 percent of a US$250 million company," he said.

He said the bank aimed to invest in companies in the media and telecommunications, in retail distribution and in infrastructure, all areas it had identified as offering huge potential growth over the coming decade.

Paribas would aim to get involved in a company three to five years before it was ready or big enough to float publicly. The bank would aim to have a board representative but leave day-to-day control of the company to the existing management.
"We are looking for companies that are already big. This is not start-up investment, not venture capital, since the businesses are already going concerns," Kokocinski said.

As a lender, Banque Paribas wanted to move away from the slower-growing European markets, where it has had a series of losses from the property markets, and move into the high growth areas of the Pacific Rim.

"The global strategy of Paribas is to become an investment bank linking the capital markets to large users of financial products. Our target clients are essentially large companies and governments," he said.

The bank was increasing the number of senior bankers in Asia to improve its business focus and expertise in key target areas. He identified these as mining and natural resources, oil and gas, media and telecommunications, financial institutions and technology.
Paribas also wanted to boost its private banking activities where it intended to focus on Singapore, Hong Kong and Taiwan.
"There is lots of new money in these areas and we would aim to be the link between rich individuals and corporations in the region," Kokocinski said.
He said Paribas had decided to move into Asia's securities markets, which was why it had purchased a majority stake in stockbroking firm Asia Equity, a Hong Kong-based company with a staff off 250.
As a result of all the changes at Paribas, the bank's Asian staff would rise to around 1,100 from 750 at present, he said.
